questions.question: When you are about to change lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to look for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for cars behind you. Just before you move to the other lane, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are in an accident, stop immediately. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles to arrive.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your papers ready before the officer comes to your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to come to you.
Get out of your car and walk toward the police car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to come to you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel when stopped by police. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: You had a bad experience at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play loud music so you do not think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release stress.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
Stop for a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, calm down before you drive. Letting your emotions affect your driving is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop at or near the accident scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another car could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help traffic move safely and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic lights. The only exception is when a police officer is directing traffic.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving:

options.text: Do not affect your ability to drive.
Help you stay alert while driving.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous because it takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: When you meet an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you do not approve of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is being dangerous or threatening, stay calm. Put distance between your car and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them or make rude gestures.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing. You do not see or hear a train. You must stop if:
questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a person signals you to stop, or a train is near or visible. If you are not sure if you can safely cross, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only found in construction zones.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give information to drivers. They help drivers position their vehicles correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming hazards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A sign with a red circle and red slash means something is not allowed. This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right of way.
Stop only if a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if a sign does not prohibit it.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Always keep your brake lights working when you drive.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before moving.

questions.question: How should you adjust your seat belt?

options.text: Buckle it snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
Adjust it to stop the seat belt warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Buckle it snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking an over-the-counter drug?

options.text: Drive anyway, even if the label warns against it.

questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. Always read the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist whether it is safe to drive.

questions.question: How can you make sure your health does not affect your driving?

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular checkups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Only drive within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your health affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Keep more distance between you and other cars.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: Driving at night is harder because you cannot see as well. Take steps to make night driving safer for you and other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means something is not allowed. This sign means you cannot make U-turns.

questions.question: When is passing not allowed?
questions.explanation: You cannot pass other vehicles on hills, curves, intersections, or railroad crossings. These places are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog. Let them cross first. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and leave extra time for your trip.

questions.question: What is important to know about trucks on the road?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
They pass faster going downhill than smaller vehicles.
They turn in a smaller space than smaller vehicles.
They pass faster going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
